analysis.title: UBS House View Briefcases - Top 10 questions answered (16 November 2026)
key_insights: UBS expects 25bp Fed hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, but says the risk of consecutive hikes has grown. October US CPI was stronger than expected: headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%.

The FOMC held the funds rate in October after a 25bp hike in September. Dallas Fed's Logan said the pace of tightening might need to accelerate. Governor Waller raised the possibility of a 50bp hike in December.
UBS does not expect measured tightening to derail US equities. It cites US GDP of about 2.5% annualized in 1H and 3.4% in 3Q, and forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose 28-29bp on the week to about 5.13% and the 2-year rose 37bp. The 10-year hit 5.36% intraday in early October, its highest since 2002. UBS rates fixed income Attractive, favoring short- to medium-duration high-quality bonds and staying cautious on the longest maturities.

AI-related stocks stayed volatile after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's surprise departure, which added to questions about AI valuations and data center investment. UBS forecasts AI capex of USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. It recommends diversified exposure across the AI value chain and warns on single-stock concentration.

Power and resources: UBS expects annual power and grid investment to reach USD 3tr by 2030. Data centers could be up to 9% of US electricity use by 2035, versus about 4% now (BNEF forecast). Longevity: global obesity drug (GLP-1) revenue is forecast to grow 12% a year through 2030.

Brent fell to near USD 95/bbl from as high as USD 118 at end-October. Brent slid 16% the prior week, its sharpest weekly fall since the pandemic. Markets are pricing more US-Iran de-escalation after a stronger-than-expected 'Blue Wave' midterm outcome, and Trump said a deal was not necessary.

The physical oil market has not normalized. Hormuz flows are near pre-conflict levels but volatile. Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure and tanker attacks keep freight high: Middle East to Asia shipping costs USD 30-40/bbl versus under USD 5 before the conflict. UBS cannot rule out renewed escalation. The IEA sees a 4Q26 oil surplus and a larger build in 2027.

US crude inventories rose 4.7mn barrels to 414.4mn in the week ended 6 November, versus an expected 1.1mn draw. Global visible oil inventories were 7.8bn barrels at end-September, more than 500mn below February levels.

UBS favors broad, actively managed commodity exposure, with a preference for copper and strategic gold. Commodities showed a 0.44 correlation with global equities and -0.04 with US bonds from January 1999 to May 2026.

Gold closed the week near USD 3,880/oz, down 4.6% and below USD 4,000. Higher real yields and a firmer dollar drove the drop. UBS forecasts gold higher over 12 months on central bank buying and reserve diversification, and suggests a mid-single-digit allocation. Q3 gold demand was 1,369t (-1% y/y) and mine production was a record 1,071t (+3%).

UBS expects major central banks, particularly the Fed, to finish hiking in 1Q27, with inflation moderating more meaningfully in 2Q. It sees faster normalization of energy supply and prices as reinforcing its 2027 disinflation view.

Equities: the S&P 500 rose 2.5% last week after a 2.7% decline the week before. Preferred US sectors are consumer discretionary, financials, health care, industrials and utilities. UBS is positive on Eurozone equities (banks, consumer discretionary, health care, industrials, IT, Germany) and forecasts 15% European earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027. Asian valuations are at multi-decade lows.

US tech came under pressure in early November on Democratic midterm gains, especially at state level, and their implications for AI infrastructure and data centers. UBS suggests using rallies to rebalance concentrated mega-cap tech positions into structured strategies with some capital preservation.

Europe: eurozone inflation rose to 4% in October on energy and food, with core at 2.5%. The 10-year Bund yield was 3.38%. The France-Germany 10-year spread hit nearly 178bp, the widest since 2011, then fell to about 150bp. Lagarde said incoming data and December staff projections will decide whether another ECB hike is needed. UBS still expects European borrowing costs to decline into next year.
Emerging market sovereign and corporate bond yields are about 7.1% and 7% (EMBI and CEMBI). UBS expects high-single-digit 12-month returns and likes EM credit and high yield.

Alternatives: UBS favors discretionary macro and low-net/market-neutral equity hedge funds, is constructive on private equity, and favors infrastructure with visible income. Global PE fundraising was USD 368bn through September, nearly 80% of the 2025 total.

Cash: UBS recommends holding two to five years of net expected portfolio withdrawals in cash and phasing excess cash into markets. US stocks beat cash in 97% of 10-year and 100% of 20-year holding periods from 1945 to July 2026. The S&P 500 has tended to rise about 10% in the 12 months after the first hike of a cycle.

risk_factors: Faster Fed tightening: Logan and Waller comments raise the risk of consecutive hikes or a 50bp move in December.
Renewed US-Iran escalation, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and tanker attacks could cause oil price spikes.
AI sector risks: capital-intensive areas face funding and execution pressure, valuations are elevated, and Jensen Huang's departure from NVIDIA adds uncertainty.
US policy uncertainty after the midterms, especially for AI infrastructure and data centers.
Elevated term premiums, fiscal sustainability concerns and AI-related debt issuance at the long end of the bond market.
France's fiscal and political situation could widen spreads further.
Energy-driven inflation in the eurozone (4% in October) could force another ECB hike.
Alternatives carry illiquidity, strategy complexity, lockup and leverage risks.
vol_and_positioning: AI-linked stocks stayed volatile after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's surprise departure. The S&P 500 fell 2.7% the prior week and rose 2.5% last week.
Hedge fund view: high stock dispersion supports low-net and market-neutral equity hedge managers, and discretionary macro has a broad opportunity set.
For concentrated mega-cap tech holders, UBS suggests rebalancing into structured strategies with some capital preservation on rallies.
Brent fell 16% in one week, the sharpest weekly fall since the pandemic.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: Trump said seeking a deal with Iran was not necessary, which investors read as lowering the chance of renewed US strikes. Middle East crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz are near pre-conflict levels but volatile.
Houthis reportedly struck Saudi Arabian infrastructure, and tankers shipping crude from the Gulf were attacked, keeping transport costs high.
US midterm elections: a stronger-than-expected 'Blue Wave' outcome fed expectations of US-Iran de-escalation. Democratic gains at state level also weighed on AI infrastructure and data center stocks.
France faces weak growth, a negative rating outlook, a fragmented parliament and obstacles to fiscal consolidation.

The UK FCA proposed letting workplace pension default funds exclude certain performance-linked fees from fee limits, widening access to private markets. Consultation ends in January and final rules are likely in mid-2027.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects measured 25bp hikes in December and March. It cites GDP of 3.4% in 3Q, S&P 500 EPS growth of 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027, and past downturns starting at least two years after the first hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Logan said the pace of tightening might need to accelerate and Waller raised a 50bp hike in December. October CPI was hotter than expected and the 10-year yield reached 5.36% in early October.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 50bp December hike or consecutive hikes beyond March, which UBS says has become a bigger risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent fell to about USD 95 from USD 118 as Hormuz flows recovered, US inventories built, and the IEA sees a 4Q26 surplus.
tension_points.bear_case: Physical flows remain volatile, Houthi strikes hit Saudi infrastructure, tankers are being attacked and shipping costs are USD 30-40/bbl. UBS cannot rule out renewed escalation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed US-Iran strikes or damage to civilian and energy infrastructure that causes price spikes.
